headline: GOLD BREAKS $4,121 AS BANK OF ENGLAND HIKES — Dollar Slides Further; Silver Lags at $52.78 as Ratio Widens to 78
snippet: Gold spot climbed to $4,121.74 on November 5 — up $60 on the day — as the Bank of England delivered a surprise rate hike that sent the pound higher and the US dollar lower, adding a second independent driver to the post-midterm dollar collapse. Silver held at $52.78/oz, underperforming gold on the session as the gold-silver ratio widened to 78, suggesting silver's near-term outperformance may be consolidating before the next leg.

headline: RADISSON MINING'S O'BRIEN RETURNS 44g/t GOLD — 9 New Holes Extend High-Grade Mineralization to 1.9km Depth; 83% Hit Rate Holds
snippet: Radisson Mining (TSXV: RDS) released nine new drill holes on November 4 from its O'Brien Gold Project in Quebec, extending high-grade mineralization to a depth of 1.9 kilometres with the best intercept at 44.18 g/t gold over 1.3 metres. The step-out program now has 137 holes completed with an 83% hit rate — a figure that holds significance for future resource classification — and multiple holes intersected mineralization in both the Pontiac and Piché host-rock groups simultaneously.

headline: PENTAGON BUYS 10% STAKE IN ALASKA COPPER PROJECT — $35.6M Trilogy Metals Deal Secures Copper, Cobalt, Germanium at Ambler
snippet: The US Department of Defense closed a $35.6 million direct equity investment in Trilogy Metals (TSX/NYSE: TMQ) on November 4, acquiring approximately 10% of the company and warrants for a further 7.5% stake tied to Ambler Road milestones or a change of control. The investment targets the Upper Kobuk Mineral Projects in Northwest Alaska — a copper-cobalt-germanium district managed by Ambler Metals, a 50/50 joint venture between Trilogy and South32 — and gives the Pentagon a board director seat at Trilogy through 2028.

headline: CITI SLASHES LITHIUM FORECAST 40% — Carbonate to $12,000/t, Spodumene to $1,200/t as Two-Year Surplus Forecast
snippet: Citigroup cut its near-term and two-year lithium price forecasts by as much as 40% on November 4, lowering lithium carbonate to $12,000/t (from $20,000) and spodumene to $1,200/t (from $2,000), citing slower battery demand growth, trade uncertainty, and consumers deferring purchases to maintain lean inventories. The bank forecasts a supply surplus persisting through 2028 as Rio Tinto's Catamarca operations and CATL's Jianxiawo mine add incremental production, downgrading Albemarle and Mineral Resources to neutral.

headline: STANDARD LITHIUM TARGETS YEAR-END FID ON $1.45B ARKANSAS DLE — Equinor JV, $225M DOE Grant, Construction in 2027
snippet: Standard Lithium (TSX: SLI) confirmed it is targeting a final investment decision on its $1.45 billion South West Arkansas direct lithium extraction project by year-end, with engineering contractor Wood already awarded the well-field EPCM contract and all major construction contracts in place. The project is a 55/45 joint venture with Equinor, backed by a $225 million US Department of Energy grant, and would begin construction in early 2027 with first production in 2029 — if financing closes on schedule.

headline: HEAVY RARE EARTHS CLEARS HERITAGE HURDLE — Radium Hill Drill Approval Now the Only Remaining Gate; 1.26% TREO Over 8km
snippet: Heavy Rare Earths (ASX: HRE) received heritage clearance for its Radium Hill project in South Australia after completing a formal heritage survey of the site, clearing the last regulatory hurdle before drill permits can be granted. Prior surface sampling across the 8-kilometre exploration corridor returned up to 1.26% total rare earth oxides plus 0.36% uranium oxide, grades that — if confirmed by drilling — would rank among the better undeveloped rare earth surface anomalies on the ASX.

headline: CAZALY ENTERS 1,118km² BRAZIL RARE EARTH PLAY — $200,000 Option Covers Uranium-Rich REE Ground in Under-Explored Corridor
snippet: Cazaly Resources (ASX: CAZ) secured a 12-month option over a 1,118 square kilometre package of Brazilian rare earth and uranium tenements for an initial $200,000 commitment, adding a low-cost entry into a jurisdiction that has attracted increasing attention from critical minerals explorers since Brazil amended its foreign mining investment rules in 2025. The land package sits within a geological corridor that hosts known rare earth occurrences but has seen limited systematic exploration.

headline: URANIUM ENERGY LOCKS IN 1.1M LB SUPPLY DEAL WITH TWO US UTILITIES — Six-Year Contracts Extend Long-Term Book Through 2032
snippet: Uranium Energy Corp (NYSE: UEC) signed long-term uranium supply contracts with two US nuclear utilities covering 1.1 million pounds of uranium concentrates deliverable over six years, adding to a growing contract book that now extends through 2032. The deals come as spot uranium holds above $92/lb and utilities accelerate contracting to reduce exposure to potential future supply disruptions — a dynamic that is widening the gap between forward contract prices and spot-market volatility.

headline: CHINA EXPLOSIVES GIANT SECURES TIBET COPPER-LITHIUM RIGHTS — Xizang Gaozheng Mamupu Deal Widens Beijing's Critical Minerals Grip
snippet: Chinese state-linked explosives manufacturer Xizang Gaozheng Civil Explosives secured mining rights at the Mamupu copper and lithium deposit in Tibet, with the company's shares surging on the news. The deal extends Beijing's consolidation of domestic critical mineral assets at a moment when Western governments are racing to build independent supply chains — and comes days before China's November 10 deadline for announcing expanded rare earth export controls.

headline: BULLION BANKS ARE QUIETLY POSITIONING FOR MUCH HIGHER GOLD — Macleod: Short Squeeze Setup as Physical Demand Absorbs Paper Sales
snippet: Analyst Alasdair Macleod argues on GoldSeek that bullion banks have been quietly repositioning their gold books ahead of what he views as an inevitable short-squeeze dynamic, as sustained physical demand from Asian central banks and sovereign wealth funds steadily absorbs the paper selling that drove gold's correction from $5,500 to $3,875 earlier in 2026. Macleod identifies the post-midterm dollar weakness as the catalyst that may finally trigger the alignment of physical and paper pricing.
